title: Uniform or Not? Uniform Motion Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A fan, a train and a bicycle are all moving, but only one could be moving in the simplest possible way. Aarav covers 5 metres every second on the flat road, then more and more every second down the slope. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 2, Motion in a Straight Line) we learn exactly what makes motion uniform or non-uniform.

Two bicycles race on a live motion bench, both covering 40 m in 8 s, while their paint marks, velocity arrows and a live x-t graph show the difference. We reason link by link why uniform motion means constant velocity, zero acceleration and a straight x-t line, compare the two side by side, and test it with two pause-and-think questions. Then a worked average speed example, the exam trap about circular motion, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Three moving things, one simplest way
0:30 What is uniform motion?
0:57 Two bicycles on the motion bench
1:42 Why a straight line, link by link
2:25 Side by side + pause and think
3:27 Worked example: average speed
4:06 Exam trap: constant speed in a circle
4:35 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:17 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Equations of Uniformly Accelerated Motion. If the velocity changes by the same amount every second, can we predict exactly where Aarav will be?
